title: I-HAB PORTABLE EQUIPMENT PANELS (PEPs)
description: The Cislunar Gateway – International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESA’s contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for Portable Equipment Panels (PEPs) in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.The PEPs are part of the power subsystem that includes a set of batteries for energy storage and a set of power management, distribution and switch units that are responsible to control and regulate the battery charging and discharging in sun or during the eclipse phase; to control the balancing of all the battery cells during the charging phase; to connect each battery to the BCDR before the Launch or during the tests and disconnect it before the removal or during the test; to connect, disconnect and distribute the primary power to other elements of the Gateway when requested; to convert the primary power into secondary power to supply the various internal loads and heaters by switchable and protected power lines.From functional point of view the IHAB EPS is composed by two main power chains. Each main power chain (PWR-CHA and PWR-CHB) is supplied by one isolated primary power domain: Primary Power Domain A1 & A2 supply the PWR-CHA; Primary Power Domain B1 & B2 supply the PWR-CHB.All the functional blocks at this level and as part of power chain A or power chain B are indicated respectively as PPDA-A (Primary Power Distribution Assembly ChA) and PPDA-B for ChB.All the functional blocks of IHAB EPS at Level 2 are indicated respectively as SPCD-A1 and SPCDA2 (Secondary Power Conversion & Distribution – ChA1 and ChA2) and SPCD-1B and SPCD-2B for ChB1 and ChB2. Each primary power domain A & B is constituted by two primary power isolated feeds named A1 & A2 for the domain A, and B1 & B2 for the domain B.The PEPs are designed to ensure common standard Gateway power and data interface for portable equipment at various locations for science and crew systems support. The PEPs will have physical, electrical and data interfaces to be accommodate in a single panel and accessible by crew. For this reason each PEP will provide one variable 3-28Vdc voltage output rated at 8 A and one fixed 120Vdc outputs voltage rated at 10 A to portable equipment via two standard power utility outlets accommodated into two identical standard circular connectors named “J1” and “J2” and one auxiliary at 120Vdc output voltage rated at 10 A to power crew support equipment (i.e. USB hubs, USB charger) accommodated into one blind-mate connector named “J3”. The PEP will also provide one data outlet for access to the Gateway Ethernet network (J4) and a set of switches, digital displays, trim resistors and LEDs. This is to provide a visual indication of the status of the power outlets and also to allow a control the power status as well as reset a faulted condition on each power outlets by crew. Each PEP communicate with the C&DH via 133 Mil bus interfaces. This is: to receive commands to control the power outlets (i.e. power ON/OFF and fault condition reset) and for setting the voltage levels of variable power outputs; to distribute periodically the internal HK data and for reporting of anomaly events and protection conditions.Further information concerning the I-HAB campaign can be found on the Agency’s website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

title: SUB-MM WAVE NOISE SOURCES FOR INTERNAL CALIBRATION SUB-SYSTEMS - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To evaluate the capability of heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) technology (such SiGe as and/or InP) as an internal calibrator noise source at sub-mm wave frequencies and manufacture a heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBT) based noise sources at two selected frequencies such as 325 GHz and 448 GHz.Description: Microwave radiometer calibration routine onboard a satellite is currently based on the measurement of external well known reference targets such as cold sky and onboard blackbody target. However, external calibration implies complex moving mechanics and long calibration cycles which are non-optimum from system performance perspective and therefore set certain limitations to instrument performance. Considerable improvements in smaller fluctuation of noise power density are foreseen by complementing or replacing the mechanically switched quasi-optical external calibration systems by internal calibration sub-systems (ICSS) based on electrically switched active semiconductor devices. Semiconductor based noise sources (cold or hot) are key blocks in these ICSS units which will benefit developments of future EO sounders and imagers on small platforms and cube-sats as well as multipixel imagers on bigger platforms. ICSS concept based active cold-loads have already been adopted in Copernicus Imaging Radiometer (CIMR). At higher mm-wave frequencies, hot load -based ICSS's are currently being developed for applications at 89 GHz and 183 GHz based on noise diodes and between 200-250 GHz based on HBTs. Development of a HEMT-based noise source is ongoing at 325 GHz. This activity aims to manufacture a breadboard of a noise source waveguide modules based on HBT technology (e.g. SiGe/InP/GaAs) at two selected sub-mm frequencies of interest for future EO instruments, such as 325 GHz and 448 GHz. The stability of the HBT-based noise sources will be compared with counterparts built on different technologies by means of theoretical assessment and experimental results where available. The HEMT technology provides advantage having the highest frequency capability as anoise source due to its high transition frequency which is already in 1 THz region. However, the anticipated advantage of HBT in comparison to HEMT is its inherently smaller fluctuation of noise power density - a key parameter for a calibrator. The recent developments in HBT technologies (both SiGe and InP) and their frequency capability open possibilities to implementation of a HBT noise source up to sub-mm region which would be a very desirable component for a stable ICSS's. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Noise source requirements definition from system level - Preliminary to critical design of a noise source waveguide modules basedon HBT technology at two selected sub-mm frequencies such as 325 GHz and 448 GHz - Manufacturing and characterization of the breadboardDeliverables: Breadboard, Report
